question.stem:
A fixed mass of a monatomic ideal gas is taken round the cycle A → B → C → A shown on the graph.

  • A → B: the gas expands at a constant pressure of $2.5 \times 10^{5}$ Pa from $1.0 \times 10^{-3}$ $\text{m}^{3}$ to $2.0 \times 10^{-3}$ $\text{m}^{3}$.
  • B → C: the gas cools at constant volume.
  • C → A: the gas is compressed adiabatically back to A.
question.diagramAlt: Graph of pressure in units of 10 to the power 5 pascal against volume in units of 10 to the power minus 3 cubic metres. A horizontal line from A at volume 1.0 to B at volume 2.0, both at pressure 2.5. A vertical line down from B to C at volume 2.0 and pressure about 0.8. A curve rising steeply from C back to A.

parts.label: a
parts.question: Show that the pressure at C is about $7.9 \times 10^{4}$ Pa.

parts.label: b
parts.question: Determine the thermal energy transferred to the gas during A → B.

mistakes.feedback: That is only the work done by the gas. The internal energy of the gas also increases: Q = ΔU + W.

parts.label: c
parts.question: Determine the work done on the gas during C → A.
markscheme: $Q = 0$, so the work done on the gas equals the increase in internal energy ✓
Allow ECF from (a); accept 133 to 145 J

parts.label: d
parts.question: Calculate the efficiency of this cycle.
markscheme: net work $= 250 - 139 = 111\ \text{J}$ (no work during B → C) ✓
Allow ECF from (b) and (c); accept 0.167 to 0.189

mistakes.feedback: Efficiency uses the NET work done by the gas over the whole cycle: subtract the work done on the gas during C → A.

parts.label: e
parts.question: Explain why the entropy of the gas does not change during C → A.
markscheme: No thermal energy is transferred to or from the gas during an adiabatic change ($Q = 0$) ✓
so $\Delta S = \dfrac{\Delta Q}{T} = 0$ (the change is treated as reversible) ✓

parts.label: a
parts.examinerNote: The adiabatic equation from the data booklet, applied between C and A (V_C = V_B).

parts.label: b
parts.examinerNote: For a monatomic ideal gas ΔU = 3/2 Δ(pV); at constant pressure that is 3/2 pΔV. No amount of gas is needed.

parts.label: c
parts.examinerNote: Students cannot integrate under the adiabat, but the first law with Q = 0 gives the work. Using the rounded p_C from (a) gives about the same answer.

parts.label: d
parts.examinerNote: Thermal energy enters only during A → B (B → C rejects energy, C → A has Q = 0).

parts.label: e
parts.examinerNote: Entropy change from ΔS = ΔQ/T; an ideal adiabatic compression is reversible.
